name: i ren / e ren (i人 / e人)
blurb: Chinese MBTI slang: i人 is an introvert, e人 an extrovert
title: i人 / e人 Meaning: Chinese Slang for Introvert and Extrovert
description: i人 is an introvert drained by socializing; e人 is an extrovert energized by it. Taken from MBTI's I and E, the pair topped China's 2023 buzzwords.
h1: What do i人 and e人 mean?
answer: i人 ("i person") means an introvert, someone who loses energy in social situations; e人 ("e person") means an extrovert, someone who gains energy from them. The letters come from the MBTI personality types: I for Introversion and E for Extraversion. The pair took over Chinese social media in 2023, and the Shanghai paper Yuyan Wenzi Zhoubao (语言文字周报) put "i人/e人" first on its top ten internet buzzwords of that year.

sections.h: Where I and E come from
body: The MBTI (Myers-Briggs Type Indicator) is a personality typology and self-reflection tool that describes preferences with four pairs of letters. The first pair is E and I. The Myers-Briggs Foundation calls them opposite ways to direct and receive energy: E focuses on the outer world, I on the inner world, and everyone uses both but usually prefers one.

Chinese users took just that one letter and added 人 ("person") to make a quick label. The weekly's 2023 list explained i人 as someone who loses energy in social settings and is generally reserved, and e人 as someone who gains energy there and is generally outgoing.

body.note: MBTI is a typology tool, not a clinical psychological test, and it cannot diagnose anything. Many free online versions circulate; treat the results as a conversation starter.

ul: 「我是i人，聚会能不能让我坐角落。」 (I'm an introvert. Can I sit in the corner at the party?)
「e人同事第一天就和整层楼混熟了。」 (Our extrovert coworker knew the whole floor on day one.)
「为i做e：为了工作硬着头皮当一天e人。」 (Going e for the job: forcing myself to be an extrovert today.)
「i人的周末：手机静音，谁也别找我。」 (Introvert weekend: phone on silent, nobody call me.)
「你看着挺e的，没想到是个i人。」 (You seem so outgoing; I didn't expect you to be an introvert.)

e人 (extrovert)

sections.h: Don't treat it as a verdict
body: Introversion and extraversion are better seen as a range, with many people in the middle and moods that shift with the situation. Joking about being an i人 is fine; using the labels to judge people or screen coworkers and dates goes too far.

faq.q: What do the i and e stand for?
faq.a: They are the MBTI letters I for Introversion and E for Extraversion. Adding 人 ("person") makes them a label.

faq.q: How do I know if I'm an i人 or an e人?
faq.a: Look at your energy: if socializing tires you and you need time alone, you lean i; if it leaves you energized, you lean e. MBTI quizzes are only a rough guide, not a clinical test.
No. An i人 prefers quieter settings and gets drained by socializing, but may be perfectly comfortable with people. Social anxiety is about fear.
